title: UNIQUE & CHECK Constraints
description: Guarantee distinctness with UNIQUE constraints, enforce business logic with CHECK expressions, and handle multiple NULLs.

data.text: **UNIQUE** constraints prevent duplicate non-null entries in one or more columns, automatically backing them with a B-tree index. **CHECK** constraints validate column values against arbitrary boolean expressions before allowing writes.
UNIQUE NULL Handling (UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT in PG 15+)

Historically in SQL, `NULL` values are treated as distinct; thus, a standard `UNIQUE` column can hold multiple `NULL` rows. In PostgreSQL 15+, you can specify `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT` to enforce that only a single `NULL` is permitted.

data.title: CHECK Constraint with Business Rules
data.content: Validating that price is positive and discounted price is lower than list price.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE products (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    price NUMERIC(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    sale_price NUMERIC(10, 2),
    CONSTRAINT chk_price_positive CHECK (price > 0),
    CONSTRAINT chk_sale_lower_than_price CHECK (sale_price IS NULL OR sale_price < price)
);

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `UNIQUE` constraints automatically generate an underlying B-tree index.
Use `CHECK` constraints to enforce business domain rules directly in the database.
Use `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` (PG 15+) when you want unique constraints to reject duplicate NULLs.
